source: EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor, six-month SUBREGION bulk files

provenance.note: Hourly PG&E-area demand; gaps/outliers filled (see counts); EIA CISO stamps shifted 1 h earlier to match CAISO load (see time_correction).

time_convention: row i = hour beginning 2024-01-01T00:00-08:00 + i h (Etc/GMT+8, no DST); hour beginning = 'UTC Time at End of Hour' - 2 h (1 h hour-ending convention + 1 h CISO label correction)

time_correction.reason: EIA-930 CISO rows run one hour late against CAISO's own load: the row EIA labels 'ending H' matches CAISO's hour ending H-1. Shifted 1 h earlier so the shape lines up with the CAISO prices and fuel mix in caiso_2024_hourly.csv.
evidence: CAISO Today's Outlook demand.csv (5-min 'Current demand', gridstatus CAISO().get_load, hourly mean) vs the sum of EIA CISO subregions: MAPE 5.6% same-hour vs 3.9% shifted on 2024-07-09 and 5.3% vs 3.6% on 2024-01-15; evening hours agree to ~0.1% only when shifted (07-09 19:00 PST 38,908 vs 38,942 MW; 20:00 37,531 vs 37,529; 01-15 18:00 26,976 vs 27,007).

Correlation of hour-to-hour changes, PGAE vs CAISO fuel-mix net supply (sum of the signed *_mw columns of caiso_2024_hourly.csv = CAISO load), before the shift: 0.72 at lag 0, 0.90 at EIA +1 h, 0.79 at +2 h; PST months 0.66 vs 0.90, DST months 0.74 vs 0.90 (a label offset, not a DST slip).
Daily peak hour, EIA CISO sum minus CAISO net supply, before the shift: +1 h on 270 days, 0 h on 47.
Cross-check: CAISO fuel-mix solar centroid falls at 11.6-12.0 PST every month, so the CAISO side is not the shifted one.

outlier_rule: <= 0, < 0.2 x median or > 3.0 x median (median 10906 MW)
